content:
How it all started # I’ve been a Linux user for quite some time now, and it’s impossible to be a Linux die-hard without encountering ThinkPads. My journey with ThinkPads began several years ago when I got my first one, a ThinkPad T480.
My ThinkPad T480 # This is where my ThinkPad adventure began. The T480 is an excellent laptop, in fact, I’m writing this part on it right now!
It’s built like a tank, but not a big tank, a relatively slim, portable tank (compared to the T420). And it has a fantastic keyboard, as all older ThinkPads do.
My trusty ThinkPad T480
New Keyboard Installation # The keyboard it came with was already really nice, but the only problem it had was that it had a German layout, and I didn’t like that CTRL was named STRG. So I ordered a new keyboard with the US layout from AliExpress and installed it. I was fairly surprised how easy it was. It took me like 10 minutes, you just remove a few screws on the bottom, and then u just push the keyboard out from the top with your fingers.
You can watch this video tutorial I followed My ThinkPad Refurbishing Project # Over the summer of 2025, I decided to take on a refurbishing project rescuing old ThinkPads. I manager to fix and refurbish 3 different ThinkPads, and then I gave up, because i got scammed by a guy on Facebook Marketplace while trying to buy a ThinkPad X270.
ThinkPad T420 # This was the first ThinkPad I had to refurbish. It wasn’t in too bad of shape, it just needed repasting, new RAM and an SSD. But boy oh boy was the teardown process a nightmare. The T420 is infamous for being hard to disassemble, and I can confirm that it is indeed a pain.
The rescue process of the ThinkPad T420
Thinkpad X270 # This one I bought from a listing saying that it’s not working. When I got it, It did turn on, but when i moved it around, it turned off randomly.
The problem that fixed it was isolating the motherboard from the metal chassis with some electrical tape. That fixed it for a bit, but then it started happening again.
To this day I’m still not sure what the actual problem was, but I think it was either a short circuit on the motherboard, or a bad battery connection.
I’m sorry to my classmate who I sold it to, I hope he can find a way to fix it.
Thinkpad X230: My Final ThinkPad # This is my latest ThinkPad project, It hasn’t arrived yet, but I’m really excited about it. I got it for 2000 CZK (80 €), which is a steal for a ThinkPad X230 in good condition. It comes with an i5-3320M, 16GB of RAM and a 512GB SSD. It also has a usb-c power delivery mod, which is a nice bonus.
What I’m going to do to it # I’m planning to do a full refurbish on it, including repasting, cleaning, and replacing the plastic parts with ones from a X220.
I’m also going to replace the keyboard with the one from a X220, because the X230 keyboard is not as good as the X220 one (you know I had to). Also I had to replace the palmrest, because I would have to file down the keyboard to fit in, and also it wouldn’t have been a perfect fit, there would be a gap at the top.
The palmrest Also had a fingerprint scanner built in, so count that as an upgrade.
How to do what I’m doing # If you want to also do this with your ThinkPad X230, I’m gonna provide you with some materials I gathered while planning this project, as well as some useful YouTube videos.
Parts needed # ThinkPad X220 keyboard ThinkPad X220 palmrest USB-C Power Delivery mod BIOS version under 2.70 (to support the mod) Keyboard mod required steps # Tip You should probably watch the youtube video instead of just following these steps, these are just so you have a general idea of what to do.
Remove the old keyboard from the X230 by removing the screws on the bottom and pushing it out from the top. Remove the X230 palmrest by removing two screws on the bottom and disconnecting the touchpad cable. Tape off components on the X220 keyboard that could potentially short circuit with the X230 motherboard. Put in the X220 palmrest into the X230 chassis, it should fit without any problems. Connect the touchpad cable from the X230 to the X220 palmrest. Connect the fingerprint scanner cable from the X230 to the X220 keyboard. Put in the X220 keyboard into the X230 chassis, it should fit without any problems. ThinkPad X230 keyboard and palmrest swap guide
ThinkPad X230 USB-C mod
title: My Story With ThinkPads

What is this? # This is a simple Linux Distro Chooser tool that I created to help people find the perfect Linux distribution for their needs. It is based on my personal experience and recommendations.
Try it out! # Find the perfect Linux distribution for you! Answer a few simple questions and get an answer, that's based on my experience and reccomendation. Start quiz Have you ever used Linux?
I'm a total beginner. I've used it for a little bit, but I fear the terminal. I know the basic commands and I'm not scared of the terminal. I have a loads of experience in Linux and UNIX systems. How much do you want to care about the stability of your system?
I just want it to work, forever, I don't want to ever have to repair anything. I am okay with fixing a small bug when updating the system or installing some 3rd party software. I'm used to repairing my system, It's a second nature to me. I know what I'm doing, my system is not gonna break, because I'm very careful and I read the wiki before every update so my system won't break. Do you care for the newest kernel and all the newest features (KDE, or other desktop enviroments' latest versions)? I don't necesarilly need the newest software, I don't want my system to break. I want the latest and newest software even if I risk my system having an issue, and I need to have the latest graphics drivers for gaming. Do you want to play videogames?
I'm a gamer and I need the best support for video games I do play games, but nothing too crazy Only supertux lol I don't care about games. Wanna see how u ended up?
Show Results Your recommended distributions: . Learn more Restart How does it work? # The tool asks you a series of questions about your preferences and needs, and based on your answers, it suggests 3 best Linux distributions for you. The questions are very simple.
Scoring System # Each distro has parameters like difficulty, stability, release cycle and gaming support, and based on your answers, the tool calculates the points for each distro and suggests the best ones for you.
Distro possibilities # Theres not many distros in the database, because I can only reccomend so much, because most distros are just copies of each other, so I only added the ones, that have the best community, and that I can personally reccomend with certain confidence.
title: Linux Distro Chooser

It would make me very happy, if you checked out my vegetarian recipe collection website called Vege Dreams.
What is Vege Dreams? # It’s a personal project of mine, where I share my favorite vegetarian recipes that I have tried and loved over the years. From Irish soda bread to Italian Spaghetti Carboanara (without bacon, of course!), there’s something for everyone.
What can you find there? # You can also find some vegan recipes there, and some recipes are very easy to adapt to be vegan-friendly, usually just remove cheese, or replace dairy with plant-based alternatives.
Where did the idea come from? # The website is actually a fork of my brothers website Tofu Dreams, which is focused on vegan recipes. I wanted to create something similar, but with a focus on vegetarian dishes, because I don’t think I’d be able to be a vegan, plus I had some of mine recipes in mind, so I really wanted to have something similar. dhonus/tofu-dreams 🌱 My vegan cooking site with original recipes. (Hugo with SEO, automatic image compression, “cooking mode” and more) HTML 1 1 How is it built? # My version of the recipe collection is styled diffrently though, I am using Bulma.io CSS framework, which i really like. Feel free to check my code on Github, and maybe even fork it for your own recipe collection! ondrejhonus/vege-dreams 🧀 My vegetarian cooking site with original recipes. (Mostly italian style foods and baked goods) HTML 0 0
title: Vege Dreams: My Vegetarian Recipe Collection

Making this website # I have made my first ever website when I was in 6th grade in primary school (I was 11). It was a very simple website made with, very coincidentally… Hugo!
How did I start? # Hugo was introduced to me by my brother, who already had some experience with it, so he set me up with a very basic template and I got to work. You can still find the website on GitHub. It’s actually my first ever GitHub repository! ondrejhonus/xyz personal website HTML 0 0 My personal website journey # Over the years, I have made several versions of my personal website, each time using something else. Before I have made this specific website, I had a website made with HTML/CSS with a CSS framework called Bulma.io.
Why Hugo again? # This time, I said to myself, “Why not try Hugo again?”. It was pretty simple, and looking at it now, after all those years, It has come a long way, and the themes actually look pretty good.
What am I doing now? # So here I am, making my first blog on my new personal website, made with Hugo and the Blowfish theme, which you can check out here.
title: Making this website
